row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that ancilla 4's mid-circuit readouts and resets disturb the data qubits enough, growing with each later measurement, that CNT2 reaches 0 in at least one of the four systems.
row.prior_work: **On every platform tried, Peres–Mermin exceeds its noncontextual bound of 4 in χ.** Two trapped ions with each observable read out sequentially: 5.46(4) (Kirchmair et al. 2009, Nature 460:494, arXiv:0904.1655). Google Willow (superconducting) with mid-circuit measurement and reset: 5.618 ± 0.005 (Kumar et al. 2025, arXiv:2512.02284; no CbD, marginal or signalling analysis). IBM Heron r2 ibm_kingston, product-only readout: 5.31, no error bars (Kelleher & Holweck 2025, arXiv:2505.21243). 2019-era 5-qubit IBM devices: about 4.99 (Laghaout et al. 2022, Eur. J. Phys. 43:055401, arXiv:2009.10751). **CbD:** the only CbD treatment of PM hardware data, Massé 2021 (arXiv:2105.13821, unrefereed; an adapted, not exact, formula), leaves Kirchmair's data contextual by 0.566; the exact CbD 2.0 LP gives CNT2 ≥ 0.141 on the same published numbers under every completion (`map/reads/p3-9-desk-work-2026-11-05.md`, `8b95dbd`). **Prior work predicts a pass for both input states.** No exact CbD LP has been applied to PM data from superconducting hardware, and no CbD analysis of sequential superconducting PM data was found (three searches, 2026-11-05, in the desk-work note, the third in another field's words: "state-independent contextuality … sequential QND … signalling disturbance correction"). **What this bet adds:** the exact CbD 2.0 LP with a CNT2 bootstrap on sequential mid-circuit-measurement data from an IBM Heron r2 (ibm_fez), in both measurement orders and for two input states; program 1's check pointed where physics fixes the answer. It is an instrument check, not a new physics claim. The engine's odds (80) sit near what the prior work predicts; the 20 points left for a fail price the device's mid-circuit measurement and reset errors, which no published IBM PM test exposed to CbD.

fields.result: On ibm_fez the exact CbD LP rejected noncontextuality in 3 of 4 systems (|00> both orders, Bell forward; CNT2 99% lower bounds 0.046, 0.038, 0.083) but not Bell reverse (CNT2 0; chi 4.40, its lower bound 4.33 > 4), resting on line R3; chi 4.35-4.69 against the simulator 5.72-5.79.
fields.verdict_prereg: fail: 3 of 4 systems contextual; Bell reverse absorbed (CNT2 lower bound 0, chi lower bound 4.334)

fields.novelty_line: **Novelty:** partly new. Both Contextuality-by-Default (CbD) analyses of quantum hardware data that I found say contextuality survives the measured inconsistent connectedness. One is Lapkiewicz et al.'s photonic KCBS data: the conservative interval is [3.127, 4.062] against a bound of 3 (Kujala, Dzhafarov & Larsson 2015, PRL 115:150401, arXiv:1412.4724). The other is Kirchmair et al.'s sequential ion Peres–Mermin data, with CNTX = 0.566 from an adapted formula, not the exact LP (Massé 2021, arXiv:2105.13821, unrefereed). Earlier work also said a disturbance-corrected test of the full sequential square was out of reach: Kirchmair et al. 2009 (Nature 460:494, arXiv:0904.1655) violated their disturbance inequality only on part of the square (2.23(5) > 2), and Gühne et al. 2010 (PRA 81:022121, arXiv:0912.4846) showed the error terms must average below 0.0417. No paper was found that applies the exact CbD 2.0 LP (CNT2) to sequential Peres–Mermin data from superconducting hardware. The ancilla/mid-circuit square on Google's processor reports only raw χ = 5.618 ± 0.005, with no marginal or signalling analysis (Kumar et al. 2025, arXiv:2512.02284), and the IBM squares give raw values only (5.3076 on ibm_kingston, no error bars, Kelleher & Holweck 2025, arXiv:2505.21243; 4.987 from products only, already worse in one measurement order, Dikme et al. 2022, Eur. J. Phys. 43:055401, arXiv:2009.10751). Ours agrees with the CbD record in three systems. It points the other way in the fourth (Bell input, reverse order), where CbD's correction for the measured disturbance absorbed a raw χ of 4.40, which fits the known excess of IBM mid-circuit-measurement error over calibration (7.98–26.1% observed against 0.72–1.0% predicted on ibmq_algiers; Hothem et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.16706). Search: WebSearch and the arXiv API (sorted newest first, checked through 2026-11), on "contextuality-by-default" (all 46 arXiv hits listed), "inconsistent connectedness", CbD + KCBS/Peres–Mermin experimental data, Peres–Mermin/Mermin–Peres/magic square + superconducting/IBM/mid-circuit, contextuality + "compatibility loophole", sequential-measurement disturbance (Szangolies, Gühne), "mid-circuit measurement crosstalk IBM", "no-signaling violation IBM quantum computer", "signaling in time" + quantum computer; 2026-11-05. claude-opus-5-5.
